dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the earnings script and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The guidance model review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Scheduled analyst calls, however aggressive, are comfortable with the script bank ready.
Prepared hostility is manageable.
Enjoyable, even, on a good quarter.
Someone new shadowed me in the IR office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the disclosure rules into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
Our earnings calls run clean because we build a scripted answer bank for every plausible question; four quarters straight without a single clarifying disclosure needed.
The bank is the clean streak.
The bank and the rehearsal of it.
Next-morning interviews after market events go fine; one evening of preparation is all it takes.
A single night converts the format.
One night is the entire difference.
I archived last cycle's notes on the guidance model and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
Securities counsel reviews the answer bank each quarter; the process has legal standing inside the company.
The preparation is institutionally embedded.
Embedded and audited.
A vendor call about the earnings script ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the IR office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the disclosure rules.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the guidance model records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The one impromptu financial-press hit I did after a market event produced a forward-looking misstatement, and we filed a clarifying disclosure within forty-eight hours.
One impromptu hit, one formal clarification.
The most expensive sentence I ever spoke.
I sketched next week's plan for the disclosure rules before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the earnings script updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The chief executive wants me doing impromptu press hits within the hour of any market event, as a standing practice.
The standing practice is the failure format.
The exact format, institutionalized.
I compared two options for the guidance model tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the IR office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
I keep routing same-hour press requests to next-morning slots and the chief executive has asked me to explain the pattern. What does my record support saying?
